Company guide of sequentially stronger earnings against a bar cut into the print after a 37% sector crash, offset by a name that has sold every print, a tax-flattered base and a disputed USD bar that caps everything small.

Teva's post-ALVO print naming SIMLANDI a top US generic and pulling its biosimilar target forward a year is the unpriced counterparty read; the FY guide needing a $300M+ Q4 is the offsetting risk and the Q3 bar is dispersed.

On-trend YORVIPATH is priced; the first quantification of 2027 R&D for the regained TransCon programmes lands on the line holders sold 9.5% in September, into a +13% 20-day run on a name that paid +2.3% for an 11.5% beat.

A real 6% weaker than the guide assumption, on a company that quantified its own FX-to-margin bridge and has no hedges, makes the 15-17% FY margin guide easier to hold at the Q4 outlook; the Q3 margin step-up is the risk, on $180k a day of turnover.

A signed $16.25 all-cash tender with no financing condition pins the stock 3.4% below the offer; the print can only move it through completion risk, and the SC 14D9 projections make a revenue miss more likely than a holdout-arming beat.

Advantech's 2.12 North American book-to-bill and Lantronix's reaffirmed double-digit FY27 land after Digi last spoke while the stock has drifted -15% with no estimate cuts and 6 of 7 prints bought; pull-forward unwind and memory costs in the first FY27 guide are the offset.

Hyster-Yale's bookings +45% and Vertiv's doubled orders, both after EnerSys last spoke, support the promised fiscal-Q3 material-handling recovery into a stock -28% since a beat, but puts are bid at +10 vol points and the sector is currently selling good data-centre prints, so the lean is small.

FirstCash's same-period print confirms pawn demand and a consensus only 1% above Q3 ignores last year's +8.6% seasonal step and a wholly owned SMG, against a group that sold beats as gold fell and October gold commentary on the call; bar unguided so sizes stay small.

The quarter is pre-released and on the bar; what moves the stock is whether a 70-75koz guide needing +32-61% in Q4 on falling recovery survives, with undisclosed Q3 AISC leaning to the top of its range.

Management's own 25-30% backlog-conversion guide does not reach the $900M revenue floor and Street FY sits above it, so a narrowing or cut is the likely guidance outcome after a +24% five-session run that has spent part of the squeeze; a record Q3 backlog print is the offset.

A 17-21% on-demand price rise live on the company's own page and absent from every preview, plus a Q3 bar below the ARR ramp arithmetic on a name whose beats were bought +34% and +15%, against the Vineland 140 MW slip risk that could trim the ARR target; crowded short and call-side skew make the squeeze the mechanism.

A +16% run to the consensus target into a first FY27 guide this company habitually sets conservatively, with a Ukraine run-rate it forecasts 'conservatively' and a CR cliff four weeks into the year, on a name that sold its last beat-and-raise; the thin FY27 bar caps the size.

First standalone print on a consolidated GAAP basis against a seed-only bar; the NT 10-Q's larger seasonal loss is mostly below the EBITDA line the bar is set on, and Brazil corn area +10.7% leans the flat sales bar slightly up.

Revenue is almost all DARPA Stage B, which was extended at ~$2.5M a quarter rather than promoted to Stage C, so the high end of a disputed $2.0-2.8M bar is hard to reach and the last two prints fell on revenue; a 23% short and a sector bid limit the downside.

Hydro Flask's owner, reporting after YETI last spoke, called the beverage category saturated and promotional with channel inventory to correct, and 139 of 202 YETI Amazon listings were marked down into fiscal Q4, while YETI's mid-single-digit Drinkware guide still needs H2 acceleration; a tariff rate below the guide's 20% assumption and a rising short are the offsets.
